cases.task: Before creating or dispatching any Job, determine which Runtime execution targets are configured and currently available, their execution profiles/provider identity, whether immutable inputs are supported, and which named immutable-input authorities exist.
cases.rawPacket: Current ChatGPT-visible Ordivon Runtime surface has these operations: artifact.read; task.cancel; task.get; task.list; task.observe; workspace.changes; workspace.close; workspace.content; workspace.diff; workspace.exec; workspace.execBound; workspace.execPlan; workspace.get; workspace.list; workspace.mutate; workspace.open; workspace.patch; workspace.patch.get; workspace.read. workspace.list lists open Workspaces. task.list lists Jobs. workspace.exec/execBound/execPlan create execution. No other Runtime operation is exposed in this packet.
cases.compiledPacket: CANDIDATE CONSUMPTION PROJECTION derived from the live owner-native Runtime catalog: runtime.describe — read-only, idempotent, no dispatch/selection/mutation. It projects current execution affordances: global execution ceiling, allowed executable roots, named immutable-input authorities, and per-target configured/available state with execution profiles, Runtime-owned provider identity, immutable-input support, structured-plan support, and Host-dependency continuity scope. Creating work remains workspace.exec/execBound/execPlan. Exact Job state remains task.get/observe.

cases.task: A conversation was replaced. Continue one known external-continuity Task from Task identity while preserving that Runtime/Git fields in its checkpoint are only navigation hints and must be revalidated elsewhere.
cases.rawPacket: Ordivon Host MCP tools: host.status; task.observe; task.list; task.resume; task.adopt; task.checkpoint. task.resume reads one external-continuity Task as TaskProjection + OperatorHandoffCapsule + WorkingCheckpoint bound to the exact Task revision. expectedRevision is an optional stale-read fence. It never validates Runtime/Git/domain truth and never invokes another system. task.observe is a compact observation; task.list lists resumable Tasks; task.adopt creates/recover an explicit continuity Task; task.checkpoint commits a new semantic WorkingCheckpoint.
cases.compiledPacket: Host consumption path: RESUME EXISTING CONTINUITY → task.resume(taskId[, expectedRevision]). Returned Runtime Workspace/Job/Git fields are navigation hints only; revalidate them with their owners before acting. DISCOVER UNKNOWN TASK → task.list. CREATE/RECOVER NEW EXPLICIT TASK → task.adopt. UPDATE SEMANTIC WORKING CLAIM → task.checkpoint. Host does not proxy Runtime truth.

cases.task: For one existing Finance goal, discover the current unresolved Finance obligations and the exact currently callable operations that could advance them, without reading kernels/SQLite/repository schemas and without mutating Finance state.
cases.rawPacket: Finance README Start here: docs/authority.md is the responsibility-to-source map; design/AGENT-SURFACE.md is the current machine-facing Finance surface; kernel/ contains canonical semantics; capabilities/ admitted operation contracts; executor/ and deploy/ execution equipment; research/ and experiments/ evidence. Package commands include finance-context-compile, finance-claim-read, finance-claim-update, finance-decision-record, finance-proposal-create, finance-execution-evaluate, finance-execution-status, finance-reconciliation-status, finance-portfolio-observe, many dataset/research/execution/venue/acceptance commands. Finance owns domain meaning; Runtime owns physical execution; Host/Harness do not become Finance truth.
cases.compiledPacket: Current Finance Agent Surface contract: finance-context-compile GOAL_ID compiles a read-only integrated Agent Context from canonical Finance state. The Context separates obligation (unresolved domain work), AgentOperation (curated callable surface), and Capability (underlying semantic/authority/effect contract). Each obligation can name targetRefs and candidateOperationRefs. Each AgentOperation exposes exact capability refs, binding/entrypoint, side-effect class, required authority, current availability and basis. It is deliberately not a scheduler and does not mutate state. Use operation-provided --describe/inputSchemaRef only after selecting a candidate operation that needs input construction.

cases.task: Before choosing a Security mechanism, determine which exposed concepts are constitutional substrate, accepted profiles, experimental integrations, or research-only/falsified apparatus. Do not run a contest, KVM experiment, or any consequence.
cases.rawPacket: Security repository exposes many entrypoints: ordivon-security-micro, evaluation/static-evaluation, cage4/cage4-deepseek, quarantine/quarantine-audit, case-snapshot, world-entity/world-message/world-resource, compensation acceptance, intent-finalization/readback/deliberation acceptances, autonomous/incentive/verifiable communication acceptances, adversarial-epistemics AE0/AE1/AE2/AE3/AE3B/AE3C acceptances, many windows-kvm build/probe/reconcile/acceptance commands, plus Python APIs. README explains that Actor request, permission, execution and world consequence are different facts. The packet does not state which individual entrypoints are stable product surface versus research apparatus.
cases.compiledPacket: Existing owner-native Python projection security_surface_manifest() returns kind=ordivon.security.agent-first-surface. Each entry carries name, tier, module, role, stability. Tiers include constitution, profile, integration, research-apparatus. The compatibility facade is explicitly maturity=mixed and presence there does not imply constitutional/stable status. Rules state that profiles do not become law merely because accepted; research apparatus may consume reusable substrate, but reusable substrate must not depend on experiment chronology; foreign Host/Harness/Runtime/World projections remain source-owned evidence. This projection is read-only classification, not an experiment runner.

cases.task: Check current World repository/machine/provider health and capability availability without creating a resource transfer, message delivery, entity migration, or changing a network route.
cases.rawPacket: World package declares one CLI: ordivon-world-doctor. STATUS says World has Cloudflare Fetch/Browser bindings, Browser bundle verification, temporal provider observations, Resource Transfer, Message Delivery, Entity Migration, WorldTaskInspector, World doctor, and operator-scoped network condition tools. Historical receipts cannot establish current Presence/reachability/provider state. README/STATUS separate provider success from Task completion. The repo also contains providers/, modules/, tests, docs and research archives.
cases.compiledPacket: World currentness surface: REPOSITORY-ONLY HEALTH → `uv run ordivon-world-doctor --repo . --offline`; LIVE MACHINE/PROVIDER HEALTH → `uv run ordivon-world-doctor --repo /root/projects/ordivon-world`. Doctor aggregates owner-native health; it does not become provider control-plane authority. Resource/message/entity operations are effect paths and are not needed for health inspection. Historical World receipts do not establish current external state.

cases.task: Compare which declared Workstation network profiles currently reach bounded destinations, without selecting a proxy target, changing the machine default route, enabling TUN/system proxy, or starting a new overlay.
cases.rawPacket: Workstation core commands include task agent:contract, agent:doctor, agent:apply, status, versions, network, network:diagnose, network:vpn, network:cloudflare-direct, network:cloudflare-test, network:transport-test, network:profiles, network:matrix, network:profile-probe PROFILE=... URL=..., dns:test, cache:report and many Windows/provider audits. The README then documents netprofile, netcontinuity, surfpath, nettopology, exterior-anchor, publicbootstrap, exterior-discovery, network-expand and network-fabric. Some commands observe; some select/admit/start effects. Global automatic routing is intentionally rejected.
cases.compiledPacket: CANDIDATE CONSUMPTION PROJECTION derived from Workstation owner semantics: QUESTION=current bounded destination reachability across declared profiles. Read-only happy path: `task network:matrix`. It returns point-in-time per-target path coverage and must not be treated as durable reachability truth. `task network:profiles` describes profiles; `task network:profile-probe PROFILE=... URL=...` probes one explicit tuple. Selection/admission surfaces such as clash-local select, surfpath run, exterior-anchor start, network-expand admit are separate effects and must not be used merely to observe current reachability.

cases.task: Before constructing a Harness Run, discover the built-in execution profile, exact no-Tool catalog/grant digests, supported CLI commands, and whether Tool-bearing CLI execution is available, without starting a Run.
cases.rawPacket: ordivon-harness --help exposes commands: capabilities, doctor, status, inspect, run, resume, recover, store-init, store-doctor, store-backup, store-verify-backup, store-restore, store-inspect, store-events. README Quick start says initialize a state root then run `ordivon-harness capabilities`; a caller supplies an exact Run Contract; Harness does not invent Objective, Context, Tool grant, Provider, budget or completion authority.
cases.compiledPacket: Harness pre-run self-description → `ordivon-harness capabilities`. This is read-only discovery of execution profiles and exact Tool catalog/grant digests. Current built-in profile is DeepSeek no-Tool; the projection also states its run/resume/recover/status/inspect commands and whether Runtime is required. Tool-bearing API exists separately; current primary CLI does not provide generic Tool-bearing execution. Do not use `run` merely to discover capability.
